Everything is saved securely in your own environment. Then it lets you:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTime-travel\u003c/strong\u003e through completed runs, step by step\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eInspect\u003c/strong\u003e every prompt, response, and token count\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSee\u003c/strong\u003e what every run, task, and step actually costs — the cost denominator for agent ROI*\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eDebug\u003c/strong\u003e failures in the built-in web UI or via MCP tools from your IDE\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eReplay\u003c/strong\u003e recorded runs offline — deterministic tests with zero API cost\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cblockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e*Coming soon: cost budget enforcement — cap what an agent can spend before it runs away with your cloud bill.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/blockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eOrchid gives your coding agent the ability to debug your AI app.\u003c/strong\u003e The proxy has a built-in MCP server, so when an LLM call is buried deep in your stack — behind a framework, a queue, three layers of abstraction — your AI assistant in Cursor, VS Code, or Claude Code can query the recorded traffic directly. No print statements, no log spelunking: ask your agent \u003cem\u003e\"why did this run fail?\"\u003c/em\u003e and it can go look, figure out why, and fix it for you.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eYou choose how much to record: route only your LLM traffic through the proxy for lightweight inspection, or capture everything for the full picture. To \u003cstrong\u003ereplay\u003c/strong\u003e a run with perfect fidelity, all of the agent's network traffic must go through the proxy — replay works by serving back the recorded responses, so anything that wasn't recorded can't be replayed.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cblockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eIMPORTANT NOTE - YOUR DATA \u003cem\u003eNEVER\u003c/em\u003e LEAVES YOUR ENVIRONMENT!\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eOrchid forwards requests \u003cstrong\u003eonly\u003c/strong\u003e to the upstream APIs your app was already calling.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eEverything recorded stays saved securely inside your own network. No phone-home, no telemetry, no sending data to third-party dashboards.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eSecrets are scrubbed in memory \u003cstrong\u003ebefore\u003c/strong\u003e anything is written to disk: \u003ccode\u003eAuthorization\u003c/code\u003e headers are forwarded untouched to the upstream but never stored, and headers, query strings, and body fields with secret-like names (keys, tokens, passwords, credentials, cookies) are stored as \u003ccode\u003e[REDACTED]\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eOne honest caveat: redaction works by recognizing field \u003cem\u003enames\u003c/em\u003e (like \u003ccode\u003eapi_key\u003c/code\u003e or \u003ccode\u003eauthorization\u003c/code\u003e), not by scanning the contents of your prompts. Prompt and completion text is recorded verbatim — that's the whole point of Orchid — so if a secret is pasted into a prompt, it will be stored along with the rest of the prompt text.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCurrent scope:\u003c/strong\u003e Built for development, QA, and staging environments. SDKs fail-soft — if the proxy is unreachable, requests forward directly to the upstream provider with no error and no data loss.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/blockquote\u003e\n\u003chr\u003e\n\u003cdiv for agent activity. It records exactly what your agents do and exposes that data as clean, local, queryable traces. Think of it as a \u003cstrong\u003eforce multiplier for your existing toolchain\u003c/strong\u003e. By providing total visibility into every interaction, Orchid empowers the AI coding assistants and SRE platforms you already use to actively understand, optimize, and debug your applications.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eNon-Intrusive Interception (Thin SDK)\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-non-intrusive-interception-thin-sdk\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Non-Intrusive Interception (Thin SDK)\" href=\"#non-intrusive-interception-thin-sdk\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eUnlike traditional LLM observability tools that require wrapping every client initialization or using heavy SDKs with AST modifications, Orchid uses an \u003cstrong\u003eAPM-style Thin SDK\u003c/strong\u003e. The SDK patches the foundational HTTP transport layer (\u003ccode\u003ehttpx\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003erequests\u003c/code\u003e in Python, \u003ccode\u003efetch\u003c/code\u003e in Node), so every LLM call made by standard client libraries is automatically routed through the local or remote Orchid Proxy — without changing your prompt-handling or generation code.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eHeader-Driven State Machine\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-header-driven-state-machine\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Header-Driven State Machine\" href=\"#header-driven-state-machine\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe proxy does not keep track of application state. It reads \u003ccode\u003eX-Orchid-*\u003c/code\u003e HTTP headers (injected by the SDK, or set manually from any language) to decide how to process each request:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003epassthrough\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/strong\u003e: Transparent reverse proxy. Forwards the request and returns the response without writing anything to disk.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003ecapture\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/strong\u003e: Forwards the request, serializes the complete request/response payloads (including streaming chunks), calculates costs, and saves them to a local SQLite database under a specific \u003ccode\u003eSession ID\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003ereplay\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/strong\u003e: Blocks all outbound network traffic. Hashes the incoming request and serves the exact matching recorded response from SQLite. If no match is found, returns a deterministic mock error.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003chr\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" Your tests now execute instantly, offline, and with zero API cost.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eBecause replay serves responses from the local recording with near-zero latency, it also isolates \u003cstrong\u003eyour own code's performance\u003c/strong\u003e: profile or benchmark your agent logic with network calls and upstream API variance taken out of the equation, and get reproducible numbers run after run.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eEmbedded Visualizer Dashboard\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-embedded-visualizer-dashboard\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Embedded Visualizer Dashboard\" href=\"#embedded-visualizer-dashboard\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe proxy embeds a React-based dashboard on port \u003ccode\u003e4321\u003c/code\u003e — nothing extra to install. Because it binds to a non-localhost address, setting \u003ccode\u003eORCHID_API_KEY\u003c/code\u003e is \u003cstrong\u003emandatory\u003c/strong\u003e when running inside Docker. If you attempt to start the container without setting \u003ccode\u003eORCHID_API_KEY\u003c/code\u003e, the proxy will crash-exit on startup for security reasons.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eExempt Public Routes\u003c/strong\u003e: The health check endpoint (\u003ccode\u003e/health\u003c/code\u003e) and the static visualizer web assets (HTML, JS, CSS) on the query port (\u003ccode\u003e4321\u003c/code\u003e) do not require the key. This allows the visualizer UI to load in your browser, but it requires the key to load any session data (the screen will prompt you to enter the key). All proxying traffic on port \u003ccode\u003e4320\u003c/code\u003e and data API endpoints (under \u003ccode\u003e/v1/*\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003e/api/*\u003c/code\u003e on port \u003ccode\u003e4321\u003c/code\u003e) are strictly auth-gated and require the key.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"docker run -d \\\n  --name orchid-proxy \\\n  -p 4320:4320 \\\n  -p 4321:4321 \\\n  -v orchid-data:/data \\\n  -e ORCHID_API_KEY=your-secure-api-key \\\n  -e ORCHID_DB_PATH=/data/orchid.db \\\n  ghcr.io/mario-guerra/orchid-proxy:latest\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003edocker run -d \\\n  --name orchid-proxy \\\n  -p 4320:4320 \\\n  -p 4321:4321 \\\n  -v orchid-data:/data \\\n  -e ORCHID_API_KEY=your-secure-api-key \\\n  -e ORCHID_DB_PATH=/data/orchid.db \\\n  ghcr.io/mario-guerra/orchid-proxy:latest\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRecording Proxy\u003c/strong\u003e: \u003ccode\u003ehttp://localhost:4320/v1\u003c/code\u003e (pass \u003ccode\u003eX-Orchid-Api-Key: your-secure-api-key\u003c/code\u003e — the \u003ccode\u003eAuthorization\u003c/code\u003e header is forwarded untouched to the upstream provider). Replayable." href="#orchid--every-call-your-agents-make-recorded-replayable"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><a href="https://orchidtrace.dev" rel="nofollow">Orchid Website</a></p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Stop digging through logs.</strong> Orchid runs in the background and automatically records every prompt, response, and tool call your AI app makes — without you having to write a single line of extra tracking code. Everything is saved securely in your own environment. Then it lets you:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Time-travel</strong> through completed runs, step by step</li>
<li><strong>Inspect</strong> every prompt, response, and token count</li>
<li><strong>See</strong> what every run, task, and step actually costs — the cost denominator for agent ROI*</li>
<li><strong>Debug</strong> failures in the built-in web UI or via MCP tools from your IDE</li>
<li><strong>Replay</strong> recorded runs offline — deterministic tests with zero API cost</li>
</ul>
<blockquote>
<p dir="auto">*Coming soon: cost budget enforcement — cap what an agent can spend before it runs away with your cloud bill.</p>
</blockquote>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Orchid gives your coding agent the ability to debug your AI app.</strong> The proxy has a built-in MCP server, so when an LLM call is buried deep in your stack — behind a framework, a queue, three layers of abstraction — your AI assistant in Cursor, VS Code, or Claude Code can query the recorded traffic directly. No print statements, no log spelunking: ask your agent <em>"why did this run fail?"</em> and it can go look, figure out why, and fix it for you.</p>
<p dir="auto">You choose how much to record: route only your LLM traffic through the proxy for lightweight inspection, or capture everything for the full picture. To <strong>replay</strong> a run with perfect fidelity, all of the agent's network traffic must go through the proxy — replay works by serving back the recorded responses, so anything that wasn't recorded can't be replayed.</p>
<blockquote>
<p dir="auto"><strong>IMPORTANT NOTE - YOUR DATA <em>NEVER</em> LEAVES YOUR ENVIRONMENT!</strong></p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Orchid forwards requests <strong>only</strong> to the upstream APIs your app was already calling.</li>
<li>Everything recorded stays saved securely inside your own network. No phone-home, no telemetry, no sending data to third-party dashboards.</li>
<li>Secrets are scrubbed in memory <strong>before</strong> anything is written to disk: <code>Authorization</code> headers are forwarded untouched to the upstream but never stored, and headers, query strings, and body fields with secret-like names (keys, tokens, passwords, credentials, cookies) are stored as <code>[REDACTED]</code>.</li>
<li>One honest caveat: redaction works by recognizing field <em>names</em> (like <code>api_key</code> or <code>authorization</code>), not by scanning the contents of your prompts. Prompt and completion text is recorded verbatim — that's the whole point of Orchid — so if a secret is pasted into a prompt, it will be stored along with the rest of the prompt text.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Current scope:</strong> Built for development, QA, and staging environments. SDKs fail-soft — if the proxy is unreachable, requests forward directly to the upstream provider with no error and no data loss.</p>
</blockquote>
<hr>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Where Orchid Fits</h3><a id="user-content-where-orchid-fits" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Where Orchid Fits" href="#where-orchid-fits"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Orchid is a <strong>capture and replay layer</strong> — a system of record for agent activity. It records exactly what your agents do and exposes that data as clean, local, queryable traces. Think of it as a <strong>force multiplier for your existing toolchain</strong>. By providing total visibility into every interaction, Orchid empowers the AI coding assistants and SRE platforms you already use to actively understand, optimize, and debug your applications.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Non-Intrusive Interception (Thin SDK)</h3><a id="user-content-non-intrusive-interception-thin-sdk" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Non-Intrusive Interception (Thin SDK)" href="#non-intrusive-interception-thin-sdk"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Unlike traditional LLM observability tools that require wrapping every client initialization or using heavy SDKs with AST modifications, Orchid uses an <strong>APM-style Thin SDK</strong>. The SDK patches the foundational HTTP transport layer (<code>httpx</code>/<code>requests</code> in Python, <code>fetch</code> in Node), so every LLM call made by standard client libraries is automatically routed through the local or remote Orchid Proxy — without changing your prompt-handling or generation code.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Header-Driven State Machine</h3><a id="user-content-header-driven-state-machine" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Header-Driven State Machine" href="#header-driven-state-machine"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The proxy does not keep track of application state. It reads <code>X-Orchid-*</code> HTTP headers (injected by the SDK, or set manually from any language) to decide how to process each request:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong><code>passthrough</code></strong>: Transparent reverse proxy. Forwards the request and returns the response without writing anything to disk.</li>
<li><strong><code>capture</code></strong>: Forwards the request, serializes the complete request/response payloads (including streaming chunks), calculates costs, and saves them to a local SQLite database under a specific <code>Session ID</code>.</li>
<li><strong><code>replay</code></strong>: Blocks all outbound network traffic. Hashes the incoming request and serves the exact matching recorded response from SQLite. If no match is found, returns a deterministic mock error.</li>
</ul>
<hr>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Key Features</h2><a id="user-content-key-features" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Key Features" href="#key-features"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Forensic Capture</h3><a id="user-content-forensic-capture" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Forensic Capture" href="#forensic-capture"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Every captured LLM call (or "Exchange") records:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Request Metadata</strong>: System prompts, user prompts, temperature, top-p, and custom tags.</li>
<li><strong>Response Telemetry</strong>: Complete completion text, usage tokens (input/output), and latency.</li>
<li><strong>Cost Calculation</strong>: Real-time USD cost attribution per session, task, and step, based on user-supplied model pricing maps — calculated at the wire, where it can't be instrumented wrong (see <a href="/mario-guerra/orchid-trace/blob/main/docs/configuration.md">docs/configuration.md</a> and the <code>/pricing</code> endpoint in <a href="/mario-guerra/orchid-trace/blob/main/docs/api_reference.md">docs/api_reference.md</a>).</li>
<li><strong>Stream Reassembly</strong>: For streaming completions, Orchid buffers SSE chunks in memory, serving them to the client instantly, and writes the fully reassembled completion body to SQLite.</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Deterministic Mock Replays</h3><a id="user-content-deterministic-mock-replays" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Deterministic Mock Replays" href="#deterministic-mock-replays"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Writing mocks for LLM calls in tests is notoriously fragile and tedious. Orchid converts mock management into a simple recording flow:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>Run your test suite once in <code>capture</code> mode to generate a JSON fixture.</li>
<li>Commit the fixture to your repository.</li>
<li>Run CI in <code>replay</code> mode using the fixture. Your tests now execute instantly, offline, and with zero API cost.</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">Because replay serves responses from the local recording with near-zero latency, it also isolates <strong>your own code's performance</strong>: profile or benchmark your agent logic with network calls and upstream API variance taken out of the equation, and get reproducible numbers run after run.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Embedded Visualizer Dashboard</h3><a id="user-content-embedded-visualizer-dashboard" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Embedded Visualizer Dashboard" href="#embedded-visualizer-dashboard"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The proxy embeds a React-based dashboard on port <code>4321</code> — nothing extra to install. Search and filter exchanges by model, provider, status, or prompt keywords; compare token usage and costs across sessions; export sessions as portable JSON fixtures.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Ask Your AI Assistant Why a Run Failed</h3><a id="user-content-ask-your-ai-assistant-why-a-run-failed" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Ask Your AI Assistant Why a Run Failed" href="#ask-your-ai-assistant-why-a-run-failed"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">When a run fails, open your IDE and ask: <em>"Why did this run fail?"</em> Orchid exposes recorded traffic through a built-in MCP server — your coding assistant (Cursor, VS Code, Claude Code) can look up the exact prompts, responses, and tool calls from that run, then correlate them back to your source code. No print statements. No log spelunking.</p>

Generate an API key</h3><a id="user-content-1-generate-an-api-key" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 1. <div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">2. Start the proxy</h3><a id="user-content-2-start-the-proxy" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 2. Start the proxy" href="#2-start-the-proxy"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Start the container and pass your generated key as the <code>ORCHID_API_KEY</code> environment variable.</p>
<div class="markdown-alert markdown-alert-important" dir="auto"><p class="markdown-alert-title" dir="auto"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-report mr-2" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M0 1.75C0 .784.784 0 1.75 0h12.5C15.216 0 16 .784 16 1.75v9.5A1.75 1.75 0 0 1 14.25 13H8.06l-2.573 2.573A1.458 1.458 0 0 1 3 14.543V13H1.75A1.75 1.75 0 0 1 0 11.25Zm1.75-.25a.25.25 0 0 0-.25.25v9.5c0 .138.112.25.25.25h2a.75.75 0 0 1 .75.75v2.19l2.72-2.72a.749.749 0 0 1 .53-.22h6.5a.25.25 0 0 0 .25-.25v-9.5a.25.25 0 0 0-.25-.25Zm7 2.25v2.5a.75.75 0 0 1-1.5 0v-2.5a.75.75 0 0 1 1.5 0ZM9 9a1 1 0 1 1-2 0 1 1 0 0 1 2 0Z"></path></svg>Important</p><p dir="auto"><strong>API Key is Mandatory in Docker</strong>: The Orchid Proxy container binds to <code>0.0.0.0</code> (<code>ORCHID_BIND_HOST=0.0.0.0</code>) by default so that it can receive network traffic. Because it binds to a non-localhost address, setting <code>ORCHID_API_KEY</code> is <strong>mandatory</strong> when running inside Docker. If you attempt to start the container without setting <code>ORCHID_API_KEY</code>, the proxy will crash-exit on startup for security reasons.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Exempt Public Routes</strong>: The health check endpoint (<code>/health</code>) and the static visualizer web assets (HTML, JS, CSS) on the query port (<code>4321</code>) do not require the key. This allows the visualizer UI to load in your browser, but it requires the key to load any session data (the screen will prompt you to enter the key). All proxying traffic on port <code>4320</code> and data API endpoints (under <code>/v1/*</code> and <code>/api/*</code> on port <code>4321</code>) are strictly auth-gated and require the key.</p>
</div>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="docker run -d \
  --name orchid-proxy \
  -p 4320:4320 \
  -p 4321:4321 \
  -v orchid-data:/data \
  -e ORCHID_API_KEY=your-secure-api-key \
  -e ORCHID_DB_PATH=/data/orchid.db \
  ghcr.io/mario-guerra/orchid-proxy:latest"><pre>docker run -d \
  --name orchid-proxy \
  -p 4320:4320 \
  -p 4321:4321 \
  -v orchid-data:/data \
  -e ORCHID_API_KEY=your-secure-api-key \
  -e ORCHID_DB_PATH=/data/orchid.db \
  ghcr.io/mario-guerra/orchid-proxy:latest</pre></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Recording Proxy</strong>: <code>http://localhost:4320/v1</code> (pass <code>X-Orchid-Api-Key: your-secure-api-key</code> — the <code>Authorization</code> header is forwarded untouched to the upstream provider). Works for LLM endpoints and any other HTTP API you route through it.</li>
<li><strong>Query API / Visualizer UI</strong>: <code>http://localhost:4321</code></li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">3. Point your app at the proxy</h3><a id="user-content-3-point-your-app-at-the-proxy" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 3. Point your app at the proxy" href="#3-point-your-app-at-the-proxy"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">To intercept and record requests, you must configure your application to route its outbound HTTP traffic through the local proxy. You can do this in two ways:</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Option A: Use the Thin SDK (Recommended)</h4><a id="user-content-option-a-use-the-thin-sdk-recommended" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Option A: Use the Thin SDK (Recommended)" href="#option-a-use-the-thin-sdk-recommended"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Install the lightweight SDK and call the initialization helper at the very beginning of your application lifecycle. This automatically patches the global HTTP/HTTPS transport clients.</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Python</strong>: <code>pip install orchid-sdk</code>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="import orchid
orchid.init() # Must be called before initializing any LLM client"><pre><span class="pl-k">import</span> <span class="pl-s1">orchid</span>
<span class="pl-s1">orchid</span>.<span class="pl-c1">init</span>() <span class="pl-c"># Must be called before initializing any LLM client</span></pre></div>
</li>
<li><strong>TypeScript/Node</strong>: <code>npm install orchid-sdk</code>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-ts notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="import { init } from "orchid-sdk";
await init(); // Must be called before initializing any LLM client"><pre><span class="pl-k">import</span> <span class="pl-kos">{</span> <span class="pl-s1">init</span> <span class="pl-kos">}</span> <span class="pl-k">from</span> <span class="pl-s">"orchid-sdk"</span><span class="pl-kos">;</span>
<span class="pl-k">await</span> <span class="pl-en">init</span><span class="pl-kos">(</span><span class="pl-kos">)</span><span class="pl-kos">;</span> <span class="pl-c">// Must be called before initializing any LLM client</span></pre></div>
</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Option B: Native Base URL Routing (No SDK / Other Languages)</h4><a id="user-content-option-b-native-base-url-routing-no-sdk--other-languages" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Option B: Native Base URL Routing (No SDK / Other Languages)" href="#option-b-native-base-url-routing-no-sdk--other-languages"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">If you prefer not to use the SDK (or are using Go, Java, or Ruby), you can configure your LLM client directly. Set the API base URL to the proxy address (<code>http://localhost:4320/v1</code>) and pass your generated API key using the <code>X-Orchid-Api-Key</code> header:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Python example (OpenAI Client)</strong>:
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="http://localhost:4320/v1",
    default_headers={"X-Orchid-Api-Key": "your-secure-api-key"}
)"><pre><span class="pl-k">from</span> <span class="pl-s1">openai</span> <span class="pl-k">import</span> <span class="pl-v">OpenAI</span>

<span class="pl-s1">client</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-en">OpenAI</span>(
    <span class="pl-s1">base_url</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s">"http://localhost:4320/v1"</span>,
    <span class="pl-s1">default_headers</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span>{<span class="pl-s">"X-Orchid-Api-Key"</span>: <span class="pl-s">"your-secure-api-key"</span>}
)</pre></div>
</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">For more configuration options and advanced setups (including cloud deployment templates), see <a href="/mario-guerra/orchid-trace/blob/main/docs/getting_started.md">docs/getting_started.md</a> and <a href="/mario-guerra/orchid-trace/blob/main/docs/configuration.md">docs/configuration.md</a>.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">4. Connect your AI assistant (MCP)</h3><a id="user-content-4-connect-your-ai-assistant-mcp" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 4. Connect your AI assistant (MCP)" href="#4-connect-your-ai-assistant-mcp"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Hook the proxy's MCP server into Cursor, VS Code, or Claude Code and your coding agent gets direct visibility into your app's recorded LLM traffic.</p>
<p dir="auto">Add the configuration below to your IDE's <code>mcp_config.json</code> (e.g., <code>~/.gemini/antigravity-ide/mcp_config.json</code> or <code>~/Library/Application Support/Claude/mcp_config.json</code>):</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-json notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="{
  "mcpServers": {
    "orchid-local": {
      "command": "docker",
      "args": [
        "exec",
        "-i",
        "orchid-proxy",
        "orchid-proxy",
        "--mcp"
      ]
    }
  }
}"><pre>{
  <span class="pl-ent">"mcpServers"</span>: {
    <span class="pl-ent">"orchid-local"</span>: {
      <span class="pl-ent">"command"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>docker<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
      <span class="pl-ent">"args"</span>: [
        <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>exec<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
        <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>-i<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
        <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>orchid-proxy<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
        <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>orchid-proxy<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
        <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>--mcp<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>
      ]
    }
  }
}</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">This runs the MCP server process directly inside the running <code>orchid-proxy</code> container, sharing its database state without spinning up a separate container instance.</p>
<p dir="auto">For other configuration options (like launching a standalone dedicated container or setting up a remote cloud tunnel), see the detailed <a href="/mario-guerra/orchid-trace/blob/main/docs/features/mcp_server.md">MCP Server Guide</a>.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">5. Specify a recording session</h3><a id="user-content-5-specify-a-recording-session" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 5. Specify a recording session" href="#5-specify-a-recording-session"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">By default, the proxy groups recorded request/response exchanges under <code>"default-session"</code>. You can organize your traces (e.g., by test run, feature sprint, or user ID) by explicitly specifying a session.</p>
<p dir="auto">The proxy resolves the active session ID using the following precedence (from highest to lowest):</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li><strong>Global Active Override</strong>: Set dynamically via MCP (e.g., calling the <code>set_active_session</code> tool) or via the Control Plane API (<code>POST /sessions/active</code>). When set, this overrides all incoming session configurations.</li>
<li><strong>Programmatic SDK Scope</strong>: Define a context block in your client application code to scope specific calls:
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Python</strong>:
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="with orchid.session("my-feature-test", mode="capture"):
    # Intercepted LLM requests here are grouped under "my-feature-test"
    agent.run()"><pre><span class="pl-k">with</span> <span class="pl-s1">orchid</span>.<span class="pl-c1">session</span>(<span class="pl-s">"my-feature-test"</span>, <span class="pl-s1">mode</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s">"capture"</span>):
    <span class="pl-c"># Intercepted LLM requests here are grouped under "my-feature-test"</span>
    <span class="pl-s1">agent</span>.<span class="pl-c1">run</span>()</pre></div>
</li>
<li><strong>TypeScript</strong>:
<div class="highlight highlight-source-ts notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="import { session } from "orchid-sdk";

await session("my-feature-test", "capture", async () => {
    // Intercepted LLM requests here are grouped under "my-feature-test"
    await agent.run();
});"><pre><span class="pl-k">import</span> <span class="pl-kos">{</span> <span class="pl-s1">session</span> <span class="pl-kos">}</span> <span class="pl-k">from</span> <span class="pl-s">"orchid-sdk"</span><span class="pl-kos">;</span>

<span class="pl-k">await</span> <span class="pl-en">session</span><span class="pl-kos">(</span><span class="pl-s">"my-feature-test"</span><span class="pl-kos">,</span> <span class="pl-s">"capture"</span><span class="pl-kos">,</span> <span class="pl-k">async</span> <span class="pl-kos">(</span><span class="pl-kos">)</span> <span class="pl-c1">=></span> <span class="pl-kos">{</span>
    <span class="pl-c">// Intercepted LLM requests here are grouped under "my-feature-test"</span>
    <span class="pl-k">await</span> <span class="pl-s1">agent</span><span class="pl-kos">.</span><span class="pl-en">run</span><span class="pl-kos">(</span><span class="pl-kos">)</span><span class="pl-kos">;</span>
<span class="pl-kos">}</span><span class="pl-kos">)</span><span class="pl-kos">;</span></pre></div>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>HTTP Header (<code>X-Orchid-Session-Id</code>)</strong>: Pass the session ID directly as an HTTP header on outbound requests. This is the primary method for custom integrations or unsupported SDK languages.</li>
<li><strong>Client Environment Variable (<code>ORCHID_SESSION_ID</code>)</strong>: Set the variable in the environment where your application runs. The SDK will automatically read this and attach the header to all outbound calls.</li>
<li><strong>Proxy Environment Variable / CLI Config (<code>ORCHID_SESSION_ID</code>)</strong>: Define the variable when starting the proxy process or Docker container. This serves as the default fallback for all incoming traffic.</li>
</ol>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">6. Configure model pricing</h3><a id="user-content-6-configure-model-pricing" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 6. Configure model pricing" href="#6-configure-model-pricing"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">To track LLM costs, you can load your model pricing definitions into the Orchid Proxy. By default, untracked models default to a cost of <code>$0.00</code>. Costs are defined in <strong>USD per 1,000,000 tokens</strong>.</p>
<p dir="auto">Here is an example payload configured with up-to-date pricing for models used in the LangGraph project:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong><code>gemini-2.5-flash</code></strong>: Input: $0.30, Output: $2.50</li>
<li><strong><code>o3-mini</code></strong>: Input: $1.10, Output: $4.40</li>
<li><strong><code>claude-3.5-sonnet</code> / <code>claude-sonnet-4-6</code></strong>: Input: $3.00, Output: $15.00</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Method A: REST API (Push)</h4><a id="user-content-method-a-rest-api-push" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Method A: REST API (Push)" href="#method-a-rest-api-push"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Send a <code>POST</code> request to the <code>/v1/pricing</code> endpoint on the query port (default <code>4321</code>):</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="curl -X POST http://localhost:4321/v1/pricing \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer your-secure-api-key" \
  -d '{
    "google": {
      "gemini-2.5-flash": {
        "prompt": 0.30,
        "completion": 2.50
      }
    },
    "openai": {
      "o3-mini": {
        "prompt": 1.10,
        "completion": 4.40
      }
    },
    "anthropic": {
      "claude-3.5-sonnet": {
        "prompt": 3.00,
        "completion": 15.00
      },
      "claude-sonnet-4-6": {
        "prompt": 3.00,
        "completion": 15.00
      }
    }
  }'"><pre>curl -X POST http://localhost:4321/v1/pricing \
  -H <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>Content-Type: application/json<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> \
  -H <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>Authorization: Bearer your-secure-api-key<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> \
  -d <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>{</span>
<span class="pl-s">    "google": {</span>
<span class="pl-s">      "gemini-2.5-flash": {</span>
<span class="pl-s">        "prompt": 0.30,</span>
<span class="pl-s">        "completion": 2.50</span>
<span class="pl-s">      }</span>
<span class="pl-s">    },</span>
<span class="pl-s">    "openai": {</span>
<span class="pl-s">      "o3-mini": {</span>
<span class="pl-s">        "prompt": 1.10,</span>
<span class="pl-s">        "completion": 4.40</span>
<span class="pl-s">      }</span>
<span class="pl-s">    },</span>
<span class="pl-s">    "anthropic": {</span>
<span class="pl-s">      "claude-3.5-sonnet": {</span>
<span class="pl-s">        "prompt": 3.00,</span>
<span class="pl-s">        "completion": 15.00</span>
<span class="pl-s">      },</span>
<span class="pl-s">      "claude-sonnet-4-6": {</span>
<span class="pl-s">        "prompt": 3.00,</span>
<span class="pl-s">        "completion": 15.00</span>
<span class="pl-s">      }</span>
<span class="pl-s">    }</span>
<span class="pl-s">  }<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span></pre></div>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Method B: MCP Tool (<code>update_pricing</code>)</h4><a id="user-content-method-b-mcp-tool-update_pricing" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Method B: MCP Tool (update_pricing)" href="#method-b-mcp-tool-update_pricing"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">If your assistant is connected via MCP, it can configure model pricing by invoking the <code>update_pricing</code> tool. The tool expects a stringified JSON schema as the <code>pricing_json</code> parameter:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-json notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="{
  "name": "update_pricing",
  "arguments": {
    "pricing_json": "{\"google\":{\"gemini-2.5-flash\":{\"prompt\":0.30,\"completion\":2.50}},\"openai\":{\"o3-mini\":{\"prompt\":1.10,\"completion\":4.40}},\"anthropic\":{\"claude-3.5-sonnet\":{\"prompt\":3.00,\"completion\":15.00},\"claude-sonnet-4-6\":{\"prompt\":3.00,\"completion\":15.00}}}"
  }
}"><pre>{
  <span class="pl-ent">"name"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>update_pricing<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
  <span class="pl-ent">"arguments"</span>: {
    <span class="pl-ent">"pricing_json"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>{<span class="pl-cce">\"</span>google<span class="pl-cce">\"</span>:{<span class="pl-cce">\"</span>gemini-2.5-flash<span class="pl-cce">\"</span>:{<span class="pl-cce">\"</span>prompt<span class="pl-cce">\"</span>:0.30,<span class="pl-cce">\"</span>completion<span class="pl-cce">\"</span>:2.50}},<span class="pl-cce">\"</span>openai<span class="pl-cce">\"</span>:{<span class="pl-cce">\"</span>o3-mini<span class="pl-cce">\"</span>:{<span class="pl-cce">\"</span>prompt<span class="pl-cce">\"</span>:1.10,<span class="pl-cce">\"</span>completion<span class="pl-cce">\"</span>:4.40}},<span class="pl-cce">\"</span>anthropic<span class="pl-cce">\"</span>:{<span class="pl-cce">\"</span>claude-3.5-sonnet<span class="pl-cce">\"</span>:{<span class="pl-cce">\"</span>prompt<span class="pl-cce">\"</span>:3.00,<span class="pl-cce">\"</span>completion<span class="pl-cce">\"</span>:15.00},<span class="pl-cce">\"</span>claude-sonnet-4-6<span class="pl-cce">\"</span>:{<span class="pl-cce">\"</span>prompt<span class="pl-cce">\"</span>:3.00,<span class="pl-cce">\"</span>completion<span class="pl-cce">\"</span>:15.00}}}<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>
  }
}</pre></div>
<p dir="auto"><strong>NOTE</strong> If you don't have a local pricing configuration, use the <code>get_pricing</code> tool to fetch the pricing schema template from the proxy. Your AI agent can then look up current model costs via web search and submit them using <code>update_pricing</code>.</p>
<p dir="auto">After updating pricing, you can backfill cost metrics on previously recorded sessions by sending a POST request to <code>/v1/pricing/recompute</code> (or calling the <code>recompute_pricing</code> MCP tool).</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">7. Load a trace fixture</h3><a id="user-content-7-load-a-trace-fixture" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 7. Load a trace fixture" href="#7-load-a-trace-fixture"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">If you already have a recorded trace fixture (e.g., from a test run or shared by a teammate) that you want to replay or inspect, you can import it into the running proxy.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Method A: REST API (File Upload)</h4><a id="user-content-method-a-rest-api-file-upload" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Method A: REST API (File Upload)" href="#method-a-rest-api-file-upload"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">If you are dealing with a large fixture, or if your AI assistant is running in a local sandbox that restricts terminal processes, you should upload the fixture file directly via the REST API. If the proxy is running locally, you must execute this command yourself in an unrestricted host terminal.</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="curl -X POST http://localhost:4321/api/sessions/import \
  --noproxy "*" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer your-secure-api-key" \
  -F "file=@/absolute/path/to/fixture.json""><pre>curl -X POST http://localhost:4321/api/sessions/import \
  --noproxy <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>*<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> \
  -H <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>Authorization: Bearer your-secure-api-key<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> \
  -F <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>file=@/absolute/path/to/fixture.json<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span></pre></div>

<p dir="auto">If your assistant is connected via MCP and the fixture is small (< 100KB), it can seed the database directly by calling the <code>import_session</code> tool over stdio.</p>
<div class="markdown-alert markdown-alert-warning" dir="auto"><p class="markdown-alert-title" dir="auto"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-alert mr-2" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M6.457 1.047c.659-1.234 2.427-1.234 3.086 0l6.082 11.378A1.75 1.75 0 0 1 14.082 15H1.918a1.75 1.75 0 0 1-1.543-2.575Zm1.763.707a.25.25 0 0 0-.44 0L1.698 13.132a.25.25 0 0 0 .22.368h12.164a.25.25 0 0 0 .22-.368Zm.53 3.996v2.5a.75.75 0 0 1-1.5 0v-2.5a.75.75 0 0 1 1.5 0ZM9 11a1 1 0 1 1-2 0 1 1 0 0 1 2 0Z"></path></svg>Warning</p><p dir="auto">Do <strong>not</strong> use the MCP tool for large fixtures. Large JSON payloads will exceed SSH stdio truncation limits. Additionally, if the proxy is running locally, AI agents cannot autonomously upload files to it using <code>curl</code> due to OS-level sandbox network restrictions blocking connections to <code>localhost</code>. In these cases, the user must perform <strong>Method A</strong> manually.</p>

<p dir="auto">Once you have pointed your application to the proxy and configured model pricing, you are ready to start inspecting traces:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li><strong>Record traffic</strong>: Run your application (or its test suite). The proxy will intercept and save all upstream LLM calls.</li>
<li><strong>Open the visualizer</strong>: Navigate to <a href="http://localhost:4321" rel="nofollow">http://localhost:4321</a> in your browser. Enter your configured <code>ORCHID_API_KEY</code> when prompted to authorize and access the session dashboard.</li>
<li><strong>Analyze and debug</strong>: Inspect your traces in real-time, view detailed token cost breakdowns, or replay execution paths.</li>
<li><strong>Explore further</strong>: Check out the guides on <a href="/mario-guerra/orchid-trace/blob/main/docs/features/session_recording.md">session recording</a> and <a href="/mario-guerra/orchid-trace/blob/main/docs/features/replay_testing.md">replay testing</a> to build automated regressions.</li>
</ol>
